cells.tense: The harvest is here now, and your hands are already in it.
cells.ask: Name one thing the last change actually produced, out loud, to someone who was in it with you. Then let them add what they saw.
cells.core:
You can see the shape of what you've been through without needing the story. That's the thing itself. Somebody tells you what happened and the pattern arrives before the details do, and you know what it cost and what it gave.

So you're looking over what the last stretch produced, and you're doing it fairly. Not keeping score. Not working out who owes what. Just seeing it, and seeing it straight. Most people can't do that with their own history — the accounts tilt one way or the other. Yours mostly don't. When you hand someone the pattern of a thing they're in, it lands because you're not weighing it in your favor.
cells.sheetLine: You can see what it cost and what it gave, and call it even.
cells.verb: gathering what the change grew, once the growing stops
cells.place: out past the literal, where the shape of the thing shows

cells.tense: You're standing at the far end of a harvest you haven't finished growing.
cells.ask: Pick one thing still in the middle and leave it there this week. When the tally arrives early, write it down and don't act on it until the thing is done.
cells.core:
You're reading the pattern ahead of the evidence. The shape shows up early — you can see where this ends and what it'll yield, and you're already totaling it up while it's still growing. The assessment has run ahead of the crop.

It's costing you the middle. The part where you don't know yet, where the thing is still deciding what it is, that part keeps getting skipped. You're not wrong about the shape, exactly. You're early. And being early means you're reacting to a result that hasn't happened, so the reacting has nowhere to land. It lands on the people around you, or it lands on you at night. Work done on nothing.
cells.sheetLine: You're counting a harvest that hasn't happened yet.

cells.tense: There's a room behind you where the pattern would have been named, and you're still not in it.
cells.ask: Take one small thing you've been sitting on and do one step in the direction it points. Not the big move. This week.
cells.core:
You haven't been picking it up. You still catch the shape of things before anyone says them — but you're not turning that on your own life. Other people's patterns, sure, you'll read those all day. Your own, you leave in the drawer.

The reading is sitting unread while the thing keeps moving. The harvest is going by. Not rotting, just going by, and you're standing still while it does. That's the whole trouble. Nothing's broken, nothing's lost, but the assessment isn't happening and the crop doesn't wait. Whatever's worth saying about what you're in the middle of stays in the drawer and the middle passes.
cells.sheetLine: You stopped reading your own pattern. It's still there, waiting.

cells.tense: You're already reading the pattern of this out loud, and calling it just how things are.
cells.ask: Say "I see what this is" about one situation you've been describing as if nobody in particular noticed it, then say what you're going to do about it.
cells.core:
You've been reading it right for a while now. The pattern, the shape of what's happening — you call it before anyone else, and you're usually correct. But it comes out as observation. Like a report from no one. As if the reading weren't yours.

It is yours. You did that. And the way you hand it over, like a fact of nature, keeps you out of the picture. Nothing wrong with being right. Everything wrong with nobody knowing it's you. When you name it as yours, people can meet the reading instead of just receiving a report. That changes what happens next. And what happens next is what you've been tracking anyway.
cells.sheetLine: You've been right about the pattern and quiet about being the one who reads it.
